title: Identity comparison with normalized representative formulas
statement: For a normalized lift of a ringed-topos morphism with a specified geometric identity isomorphism and its compatible structural ring map, there are ordinary and derived pullback isomorphisms to the identity, normalized by scalar insertion and componentwise chain maps on flat-term K-flat complexes, and compatible with tensor and unit. Their ordinary and derived right mates are normalized by the ordinary identity and the right-derived unit formula on every complex. The recorded presentations, edges, representative models and normalization equations are those defined in [def-sfb-ringed-derived-comparison-data].

source.place: Identity case of Tags 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition) and 07A6; original comparison proof step 11

proof.text: 1. Use the geometric identity isomorphism to transport underlying module sections. The structural-ring-map equation makes this transport linear, so the module-linear Hom equivalence of the morphism lifts it to an ordinary direct-image isomorphism. Take its left adjunction mate using the normalized adjunction and identify scalar insertion through the geometric Hom equivalence.

2. Map the ordinary right mate componentwise to complexes. Its composite with localization is naturally isomorphic to localization, hence the identity derived functor is right derived. Right-derived uniqueness gives the right comparison and its unit formula on every complex. Take its left adjunction mate. Extend the supplied canonical transpose equation from K-injective targets to arbitrary targets by a K-injective resolution and naturality; at the ordinary identity chain map this proves the asserted pullback formula on flat-term K-flat sources.

3. The insertion normalization and the canonical ordinary tensor formula show on pure sections that ordinary tensor pullback followed by the comparison equals the tensor of the two ordinary comparisons. Apply total-complex extensionality and check every bidegree summand to obtain the corresponding chain-map identity.

4. For two flat-term K-flat representatives their total tensor is again flat-term K-flat. Convert between site flatness and categorical tensor flatness using siteSheafTensorRightIso. Apply the canonical derived tensor representative equation, the chain-map identity in step 3, and naturality of the representative tensor isomorphism to identify the tensor equation after the derived comparison. Cancel the image of the representative isomorphism. Choose flat-term K-flat resolutions of arbitrary derived objects and transport the equation along their isomorphisms by naturality. The monoidal left-unit law and the faithfulness of tensoring by an object isomorphic to the unit imply the unit equation.

proof_origin.place: Identity cases of Tags 0D6D, 0D6E and 07A6; F4 formal proof by ordinary linear transport, right-derived uniqueness and adjunction mates, K-injective naturality, and K-flat tensor representatives.
